pages.title: Implementation and maintenance guide
pages.purpose: How files-to-prompt traverses inputs, handles hidden files and ignore rules (.gitignore and --ignore), formats output, handles errors, plus a focused maintenance guide grounded in the implementation and tests.
instructions: Cover: path collection from args+stdin, os.walk traversal order and per-directory pruning, hidden-file default exclusion, .gitignore rule accumulation (parent dirs plus each visited dir) and fnmatch basename matching, --ignore pattern matching incl. --ignore-files-only, extension filter semantics, output writers (default, cxml with global index, markdown with backtick length logic and EXT_TO_LANG), UnicodeDecodeError handling, and the output-file writer.
Ground every non-obvious claim in source or tests with repo:// citations; state uncertainty where evidence is absent.

Include a focused maintenance guide: where each behavior lives (functions/line ranges), which pytest tests pin each behavior, and caveats (e.g. global_index module state, endswith extension matching).

pages.title: Quickstart
pages.purpose: Installation and practical CLI usage of files-to-prompt: inputs (arguments and stdin), filtering options, default/XML/Markdown output formats, line numbering, and writing output to a file.
instructions: Cite concrete source evidence (repo:// spans in files_to_prompt/cli.py or tests) for non-obvious behavior; do not invent guarantees.

Cover installation via pip (and the files-to-prompt console entry point), basic invocation with one or more paths, stdin input including --null, -e extensions, --ignore and --include-hidden filtering, default --- separator output, --cxml XML output, --markdown fenced output with language guessing and backtick escaping, -n line numbers, and -o output file.
Keep to 400-600 words; concise and practical, not a README dump.
